newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread's Jarvis to head low pay unit - FT.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread's Jarvis to head low pay unit - FT.

text.p: Peter Jarvis, due to step down next month as chief executive of brewer to leisure group Whitbread Plc, will head the new body to advise on the level of Britain's planned minimum wage, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.
The newspaper said the choice was a surprise given Jarvis' advocacy of a system of regional minimum wages, which the governing Labour Party has ruled out.
Jarvis was recently opposed to a minimum wage but softened his position following talks with Ian McCartney, the minister in charge of labour market reforms.
Government advisers told the newspaper it was always the plan to appoint a businessman to head the low pay commission.
"The job of the commission will be to win over business, and as a reformed sceptic Peter Jarvis is ideal," one official was reported as saying.
David Thomas takes over from Jarvis as Whitbread's chief executive in June.
Jarvis is the second appointment of a top 100 company head by the new Labour government. It has given a ministerial role to former British Petroleum Co Ltd head Sir David Simon
